abstract: Connectomics, the comprehensive mapping of neural circuits at nanoscale resolution, has historically relied on electron microscopy (EM), both transmission (TEM) and scanning (SEM). However, as connectomics scales towards larger brain volumes and whole mammalian brains, substantial technical challenges emerge. Here, we highlight key challenges and advancing approaches that hold promise, particularly those that integrate three-dimensional, multi-resolution, and time-resolved imaging to capture both long-range and local wiring, down to supramolecular resolution.
